page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance in the ecs.c6 family, designed for high compute density per gigabyte of memory. Based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM virtualization, the instance features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Hardware resources include 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, coupled with 48 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU). Network performance is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The configuration includes zero GPUs and no local SSD storage, necessitating network-attached storage for disk operations.

Hardware acceleration capability includes AVX-512 with VNNI extensions, AES vector cryptography, and FMA instructions. Benchmark metrics indicate a distinction between single-threaded and multi-threaded performance. Single-core performance tests such as stress-ng and gzip compression fall into lower percentiles. Conversely, multi-core metrics perform in average ranges, demonstrated by a multi-core stress-ng score of 21007.3, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8967.0, and a PassMark CPU rating of 21643.62. Memory read throughput reaches up to 1168.35 GB/sec for cached blocks and 108.94 GB/sec for uncached blocks, supporting steady data throughput.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides effective cost efficiency for CPU-bound execution environments where high thread density is required without paying for excess RAM capacity. Primary tradeoffs involve the lack of onboard storage and lower single-thread efficiency, making workload scaling reliant on multi-threading. The instance is structured for parallel processing tasks, including CI/CD software compilation, static web serving, Redis caching nodes, data transformation pipelines, and general multi-threaded compute workloads.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.6xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture under KVM virtualization, it provides 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores, 48 GB of system memory, and an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance includes hardware vector accelerations such as AVX-512 VNNI alongside AES cryptography instructions. It contains no dedicated GPU hardware or local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate average multi-core CPU and memory throughput, such as a PassMark CPU score of 21643.62 and Redis SET throughput exceeding 20 million operations per second, contrasted with weaker single-core processing metrics. The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation offers efficient compute density for parallelized tasks, making this server well suited for multi-threaded batch jobs, software compilation with Clang, ETL workloads, and high-throughput static web serving.
